stimulus.text: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796: “It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.” Washington also warned, in the most solemn manner, against “the baneful effects of the spirit of party generally,” saying it “serves always to distract the public councils and enfeeble the public administration.” The address was published in a Philadelphia newspaper, not delivered as a speech, as Washington left office after two terms.
stimulus.source_note: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quotes George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796, public domain.
stem: According to Washington, what did “the spirit of party” do to the government?

options.text: It distracted public councils and weakened the administration.
It made the president stronger than Congress.
options.misconception: Washington said party spirit weakened government, not that it strengthened the president.

options.text: It ended all debate between the Federalists and the Democratic-Republicans.
options.misconception: Party spirit fed the debate between the parties, it did not end it.

options.text: It forced the states to give up their militias.
options.misconception: Washington said nothing about party spirit and the militias.

rationales.A: Washington’s words in the stimulus say party spirit distracts the public councils and enfeebles the public administration.
rationales.B: Washington said party spirit weakened government, not that it strengthened the president.
rationales.C: Party spirit fed the debate between the parties, it did not end it.
rationales.D: Washington said nothing about party spirit and the militias.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus quotes Washington warning against the baneful effects of the spirit of party.
2. He says it distracts the public councils and enfeebles the public administration.
3. In plain words, parties pull leaders toward their own side and away from the common good.
4. So party spirit weakened government rather than strengthening it or ending debate.
Remember: when a quote names the effect, use the quote’s own words as the answer.
